title: Declaring Generic Impls
goal: Fix the impl declaration so the struct supports generic and type-specific methods.
hints: The compiler needs to know whether T in impl Hold<T> is a generic variable or a specific concrete struct.
To target a method specifically to Hold<String>, place String inside Hold<...>.
explanation: `impl<T>` brings the generic parameter `T` into scope for the implementation block. Omitting `<T>` causes `E0412` because Rust treats `T` as an undeclared concrete type. Adding `Copy` to `s1` fails with `E0277` because `String` is not `Copy`. Explicitly using `impl Hold<String>` defines `.speak()` exclusively for `Hold<String>`, whereas placing `i32` causes `E0308` because `&i32` cannot be returned as `&str`.
